question: Why does Nick Turley think natural language matters for AI interfaces, while turn-by-turn chat may not be the long-term solution?
expected_points: Natural language is a natural way for people to communicate with software.
Chat was the simplest way to launch ChatGPT, not necessarily the best lasting interface.
AI could offer other interfaces, such as rendering its own UI or working within existing apps.
evidence_quote: I think natural language is here to stay, but this idea that it has to be a turn-by-turn chat interaction I think is really limiting.

sections.heading: Why natural language matters
sections.content: Turley says natural language is the most natural form of human communication, so it matters that people can communicate with software that way. [S1]

sections.heading: Why chat may not be the long-term interface
sections.content: He distinguishes natural language from chat: turn-by-turn chat was simply the easiest way to ship at the time, and he is surprised that so many products copied that pattern instead of trying other ways to interact with AI. He calls chat limiting as an end-all interface: it can make people feel they are talking to a person, and funneling all software use through a chatbot seems restrictive and even dystopian to him. He points to AI rendering its own UI and to people continuing to use products such as Figma and Google Docs as reasons to explore interfaces beyond chat. [S1, S2]
